Getting started with pkgdossier

Source: vignettes/pkgdossier.Rmd
pkgdossier.Rmd

A package’s tests check that each version is consistent with itself. They do not check what a user of the last release meets after upgrading: the code from the vignettes and the help pages they learned from, run unchanged under the new version. pkgdossier runs that code under both versions, each installed in its own library and run in its own R process, and lists every difference with a mechanical label. It does not decide whether a difference is intended; it gives you the evidence and the NEWS bullets that might explain it.

A first dossier

pkgdossier ships a tiny package, udfixture, in two versions with one planted difference of each kind. example_dossier() describes a comparison of the two; like dossier(), it only describes, and nothing is installed yet.

library(pkgdossier)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'pkgdossier'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     step
d <- example_dossier()
d
#> <pkgdossier dossier> udfixture
#>   base:      tarball /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/pkgdossier/extdata/udfixture_1.0.0.tar.gz
#>   candidate: tarball /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/pkgdossier/extdata/udfixture_1.1.0.tar.gz
#>   scenarios: baseline vignettes; baseline help-page examples; scenario file /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/pkgdossier/extdata/udfixture-scenarios.R
#>   runs:      abba, 3 timed repeats per timed step, seed 20261027 set per step
#>   capture:   width 80, 100 dpi, LANGUAGE en
#>   collect:   default caps; default skipped classes
#>   deps:      shared, from the current library paths
#>   work:      /tmp/Rtmpl1rXu9/pkgdossier-example

run_dossier() runs the stages in turn: prepare_versions() installs both versions into the work folder, run_scenarios() runs the scenarios four times (baseline, candidate, candidate, baseline), and compare_runs() compares the runs. It then writes the HTML report and the JSON. Each stage caches its work, so a second call after changing the candidate rebuilds and reruns only the candidate.

cmp <- run_dossier(d, html = file.path(tempdir(), "dossier-page"), open = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
cmp
#> <pkgdossier comparison> udfixture 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0
#> 3 scenario(s), 28 step(s) compared, 2 not run; abba runs, 3 timed repeats per timed step

Reading the differences

Each difference has one kind, with a severity for sorting: 1 for code that breaks (a new error, a removed element), 2 for results that move, 3 for output, plots and timing, 4 for additions and fixes. unstable (0) marks a step whose two runs under one version disagree, so it cannot be compared.

differences() returns them as a data frame to filter:

diffs <- differences(cmp, max_severity = 2)
diffs[, c("step", "kind", "path", "base", "cand")]
#>             step                    kind     path
#> 1          noisy                unstable     <NA>
#> 2         result           field_removed    res$b
#> 3          check               error_new    error
#> 4  extend_result   argument_new_required     keep
#> 5      warn_gone        argument_removed  verbose
#> 6       estimate             value_moved est$main
#> 7          ex-01             value_moved est$main
#> 8          ex-02             value_moved  (value)
#> 9       warn_new             warning_new  warning
#> 10    warn_class condition_class_changed  warning
#> 11     err_class condition_class_changed    error
#> 12         label             value_moved      lab
#> 13        report         default_changed   digits
#>                               base                          cand
#> 1             differs between runs          differs between runs
#> 2                             <NA>                          <NA>
#> 3                             <NA>         `x` must be character
#> 4                             <NA>                    (required)
#> 5                             TRUE                          <NA>
#> 6                              0.5                           0.6
#> 7                              0.5                           0.6
#> 8                              0.5                           0.6
#> 9                             <NA>       results may be unstable
#> 10 simpleWarning/warning/condition slowWarning/warning/condition
#> 11     simpleError/error/condition    inputError/error/condition
#> 12                           alpha                          beta
#> 13                               2                             3

summary() has one row per step:

s <- summary(cmp)
head(s[, c("scenario", "step", "status", "kinds", "news")], 10)
#>       scenario     step  status                       kinds news
#> 1        intro    setup    same                                0
#> 2        intro chunk-02    same                                0
#> 3        intro estimate changed                 value_moved    1
#> 4        intro   report changed              output_changed    1
#> 5        intro     draw changed                plot_changed    0
#> 6        intro     data    same                                0
#> 7        intro expected    same                                1
#> 8  ex_estimate    ex-01 changed                 value_moved    1
#> 9  ex_estimate    ex-02 changed output_changed, value_moved    1
#> 10 ex_estimate    ex-03    same                                1

NEWS candidates

For each step, pkgdossier reads the candidate’s NEWS from the sections written after the baseline’s version and attaches the bullets that name a function the step uses. A difference in a step that no bullet names gets no_news = TRUE: a change users will meet that the NEWS may not tell them about.

named <- differences(cmp, no_news = FALSE)
named[, c("step", "kind", "news")]
#>       step           kind
#> 1    check      error_new
#> 2 estimate    value_moved
#> 3    ex-01    value_moved
#> 4    ex-02    value_moved
#> 5   report output_changed
#> 6    ex-02 output_changed
#>                                                                       news
#> 1       `check_input()` now requires character input and errors otherwise.
#> 2                   `estimate()` returns a main estimate of 0.6 (was 0.5).
#> 3                   `estimate()` returns a main estimate of 0.6 (was 0.5).
#> 4                   `estimate()` returns a main estimate of 0.6 (was 0.5).
#> 5 Printed reports show the version in their heading (`print.ud_report()`).
#> 6                   `estimate()` returns a main estimate of 0.6 (was 0.5).
nrow(differences(cmp, no_news = TRUE))
#> [1] 18

This is a search, not a judgement: a bullet can name a function without covering the change, and a change can be covered by a bullet in other words.

Writing it up

The report (write_dossier_html()) is a folder that opens in any browser without a network: provenance of both versions, the labelled differences, and per step the side-by-side output, the numbers that moved and the plot pairs. write_dossier_json() writes the same data as JSON. write_dossier_md() writes a short summary for a pull-request comment:

cat(write_dossier_md(cmp))

pkgdossier: udfixture 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0

The package ships a GitHub Actions workflow that runs a dossier of the CRAN release against each pull request and posts this summary: system.file("github", "pkgdossier.yaml", package = "pkgdossier").

Your own package

In your package’s folder, one call makes the dossier:

run_dossier()

It compares the folder with the package’s CRAN release, running the release’s vignettes and help-page examples under both, and is the same as run_dossier(dossier("mypkg")): only the package’s name is read from the folder. It asks before downloading, opens the report, and prints the comparison, starting with a one-line verdict. When it cannot start, it says why and what to write instead: outside a package folder it names the package nearby; for a package not on CRAN yet it names the repository’s tags (base = git_ref(".", "v0.3.0")); for a missing dependency it gives the install.packages() line. A step that hangs is stopped after step_timeout (5 minutes for one execution) and recorded, and a step that crashes R is recorded too. Call it again after a change: what has not changed is reused, and only the candidate is rebuilt and rerun (its timings are then shown but not labelled, as they were not made alongside the baseline’s).

As a user of a package rather than its maintainer, compare the version you have with the current release before upgrading: run_dossier(dossier("ggplot2", base = installed_version(), candidate = cran_release())). A version installed from GitHub or R-universe has no CRAN source, and the call says what to write instead.

To say more, describe the dossier: where both versions come from and which code to run. Scenario files add code neither the vignettes nor the examples cover.

d <- dossier("mypkg",
  base = cran_release(),                       # or cran_version("1.2.0"), tarball()
  candidate = git_ref("path/to/mypkg", "main"), # or local_path("path/to/mypkg")
  scenarios = list(from_vignettes(), from_examples(),
                   scenario_file("dev/dossier/scenarios.R")),
  work = file.path(tempdir(), "dossier-mypkg")
)
cmp <- run_dossier(d)

Everything that shapes the runs (reps, the seed, the console width, the dependencies and so on) is set in dossier(), and print(d) shows it. The stages take only how they run, such as step_timeout and workers, and compare_runs() takes the tolerances: changing one only compares again. A setting given to the wrong function is an error that writes out the right call, and cmp$dossier is the dossier a comparison was made from.

A scenario file uses scenario() and step(). Steps in one scenario share an environment, so later steps see what earlier steps created:

scenario("basics", title = "Linear model", source = "README",
  step("setup", "setup", d <- head(mtcars, 20)),
  step("fit", "fit", fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = d)),
  step("coef", "print", coef(fit), values = TRUE),
  step("plot", "plot", plot(d$wt, d$mpg), w = 5, h = 4)
)

By default both versions use the dependencies in your library, so differences come from the package alone; prepare_versions() says before installing if a version needs a dependency you do not have. With dossier(..., deps = deps_cran()) it instead installs the current CRAN versions of every dependency into the work folder, as a new user installing today would get them, and with deps_snapshot() the versions CRAN had when the baseline was released (see ?deps). Downloads happen only in prepare_versions(), which says what it fetches and asks first in an interactive session.
